title: One Stroke, No Undo — The Art of Chinese Calligraphy | China Travel Expert
description:
In Chinese calligraphy there's no eraser and no undo — the ink hits the paper once, and every mistake stays.

The whole art runs on the "Four Treasures of the Study": brush, ink, paper and inkstone. The brush never lands the same way twice, which is why the greatest pieces can't be reproduced. In 353 CE, a little drunk at a spring gathering, Wang Xizhi dashed off the Orchid Pavilion Preface — still celebrated as China's finest running script. Legend says that once he sobered up, he could never match it again.

🧭 Expert Tip: If you try calligraphy in China, ask for xuan paper (宣纸) — it drinks ink like nothing else and is what the masters actually use.

一笔落下，无法重来——这就是中国书法。
